chapter: Leaving New York, jazz styles and religion
title: A rolling stone gathers no moss
summary: Smith would have gone home even if famous, citing religious advice about rolling stones and the strain of road life on a marriage.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Supposing that you'd been making more money. Supposing that you'd become a star, say, a little bit along the lines of Coleman Hawkins or someone like that. You presumably would not have come home, do you think?
Oh yeah, yeah. I sure would have.
Yeah, I came home and went in business.
Even if you'd have been famous you would have come home?

Yeah. Oh yeah. Sure would have. Yeah, I came home and went in business. If I'd have made a lot of money, I'd have come home and done the same thing. Yeah, I got tired of running up and down the road so much. And I knew they couldn't pay us always. A lot of the people I used to room with... I'd travel around and stay two or three days with people, and talk, and they'd find out I was a musician and whatnot, and they'd give me advice that always rang in my ear. And it was Christian people. They said, "A rollin' stone never gather no moss." And I'd think ...(? )...(? )...
Do you think that they were meaning that in the religious sense?
Yeah, yeah. And the thing about traveling... "A rolling stone never gather no moss" mean that you're running

there, traveling around, and you stay on your (?) all the time -- ain't no one chasing you to get nothing. No. Couldn't hardly keep a family, running around! Your wife, she'd get tired of following you, and then a lot of times she couldn't follow you. And I didn't have no transportation for myself, until right at the end there around Kansas City I bought me a car. But most of the time I had to ride the other man. I'd want to come home for a little vacation, and I was too poor -- couldn't do it. So I just got tired of it.
